### This is a beta release

This build is for testing only. It is published as a pre-release, so it is not offered to
existing installations through the in-app updater — install it by hand from the assets below,
and keep the stable release around if you need to go back.

### Highlights

- Automatic port detection for paired hosts: the port a host occupies no longer has to be picked
  by hand. A host announces its own port whenever that value changes while it is on screen, so its
  peers fill the field in with no interaction at all. Startup also asks every paired host once, for
  a computer that was off when that announcement went out.
- Only a host that is on screen can vouch for its own port, because DDC reports the input a display
  is *showing*, never which port the reader occupies. A confirmed report corrects a port you set
  earlier; an unconfirmed one only fills an empty field and never overwrites your choice.
- "Test connection" now adopts whatever the host reports and says what happened, including why a
  port stayed empty. The previous path filled the field in only at the moment a host was added, and
  failed silently.

### Known limitations

- Automatic detection only works between hosts running this version. Older hosts ignore the new
  notice, so their port still has to be set by hand.
- The macOS DMG is ad-hoc signed but not notarized with an Apple Developer ID, so Gatekeeper may
  require manual approval.

### What to test

- Add a host and confirm its port fills itself in without being picked.
- Switch a display to another host and confirm the port that host reports is the one it occupies.
- Run "Test connection" against a host that is off, and confirm the message explains why the port
  stayed empty.
